newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money edges up, bond prices stable.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money edges up, bond prices stable.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged higher to 13.0/13.5 percent from 9.5/10.0 percent on Wednesday, while bond prices were stable, dealers said.
They said overnight money was apparently driven up by rises in short-term swaps despite sufficient rupiah supply.
One local bank dealer said the market was still haunted by liquidity concerns, with some speculating on ample condition on Friday due to large amounts of maturing papers (SBIs).
"But some seem to rely on a tight scenario because of the month-end factor and weekly tax payments." he said.
"Operators appear to be confused over which could be the likely scenario. As a result, the rates are mixed," he said.
Dealers said longer-term rates remained stable.
One- and three-month money were at 13.25/13.50 and 13.50/13.75 percent, respectively.
Overnight swap was at 0.5/0.6 and tom/next at 0.6/0.7.
Longer-term swap rates were little changed from Tuesday.

The central bank kept its rates for bilateral papers (SBIs) stable on Wednesday. Bank Indonesia offered 5-6 day SBIs at eight percent, seven-day at nine percent, two-week at 10.0 percent, three-week at 10.5 percent, one- and three-month at 11.25 and 12.00 percent.
One state bank dealer said the weekly SBIs auction of 300 billion rupiah was done at 12.0 percent, suggesting further sufficient liquidity supply in the money market.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 13.55 percent, compared with 12.51 percent on Monday.
Bond dealers said prices remained stable, with sustained demand, but not as hot as last week.
One bond dealer at a foreign bank said he was looking for some good names but it was difficult to find reasonable lines.
"I'm looking for Astra and PLN V/A bonds. But people would rather hold them back at present," the dealer said.
He said the market was also looking at the $150 million five-year medium-term notes of PT Semen Gresik which was placed mainly offshore.
"Overall response seems to be good," the dealer said.
Another bond dealer said the grey market price of the five-year 400 billion rupiah straight bonds of PT Astra International declined by 25 basis points to 100.25 percent on Wednesday morning.
"I think it might be due to some liquidity tightening in the money market. We see some increases in the swap market," the dealer said.
Dealers said the yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was steady at 15.37 percent at the price of 105.25 percent.
